name: Touch events and touch point count
plain: Reports finger positions and the number of touch points the device supports.
meaning: navigator.maxTouchPoints separates phones, tablets and touch laptops from plain desktops, a common fingerprint input. Touch radius and force add small device level detail.

web.api: touchstart/move/end; Touch.radiusX, radiusY, force; navigator.maxTouchPoints; 'ontouchstart' in window

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Events go to the touched frame
steps: Page reads clientX, clientY, radiusX and force

limits.headline: Can see your finger touches and how many touch points your device supports
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you touch the screen, and the touch count is checked on load
can: See where and when your fingers touch the page
Tell a phone, tablet or touch laptop apart from a plain desktop
Learn small details like touch size where supported
cannot: See touches on other pages or apps
See touches while the page is in the background
Work in desktop Safari, which does not have touch events
limits.differs: Chrome, Firefox and Safari on iPhone support them. Safari on Mac does not.

story.what_it_is: The page sees finger touches and how many touch points your device supports.

marketing.name: Touch events
marketing.pitch: Describes events for touch screens that tell pages when and where fingers touch, move and lift.

story.for_you: You tap, swipe and pinch and the page responds. You do not see that the site also learned how many fingers your device can track. That number helps it tell a phone from a laptop.
story.for_makers: Touch drives mobile games, maps and drawing. The touch point count also helps sites guess device type and block fake browsers, so it shows up in fingerprints.

use_cases.example: A mobile browser game turns finger drags into movement and taps into actions, with several fingers at once.
A cloud gaming site draws on screen controller buttons for touch players.
A web map lets you pinch to zoom and two finger rotate.
A drawing app supports multitouch gestures for zoom and undo.
A site checks touch points to split phone, tablet and desktop traffic.
A fraud check flags a browser that claims to be a phone but reports zero touch points.

technical_bounds: maxTouchPoints is 0 on no touch hardware, commonly 5 on phones, 10 on tablets and laptops (up to 20 on some)
TouchEvent constructors exist only on touch capable devices in Chromium; Safari desktop has no TouchEvent
force is 0 to 1 where hardware supports it; radius may be 0 on devices that do not report contact area
touchstart and touchmove listeners on window default to passive in Chrome 56 and Safari 11.1 (cannot cancel scroll)
Cannot read touches outside the page or on the browser UI

history.change: Document level touch listeners passive by default
